extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering data set where questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results, and annotates a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page, or marks null if no long/short answer is present.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.citeAs: Kwiatkowski, T., Palomaki, J., Redfield, O., Collins, M., Parikh, A., Alberti, C., Epstein, D., Polosukhin, I., Devlin, J., Lee, K., Toutanova, K., Jones, L., Kelcey, M., Chang, M.-W., Dai, A. M., Uszkoreit, J., Le, Q., & Petrov, S. (2019). Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 7, 453–466. https://doi.org/10.1162/tacl_a_00276
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotators mark null if no long/short answer is present on the page. 51% of examples have no answer labeled and are not discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine and Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Simple heuristics are used to filter questions from the query stream. Queries are 8 words or more and match specific syntactic patterns (e.g., start with 'who', 'when', 'where'). Questions are run through the Google search engine and kept only if a Wikipedia page is in the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators are presented with a (question, Wikipedia page) pair and return a (long answer, short answer) pair. The task is divided into three stages: Question Identification (determining if the question is good or bad), Long Answer Identification (selecting the earliest HTML bounding box containing the answer), and Short Answer Identification (selecting the entity or set of entities within the long answer).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: There is often genuine ambiguity in whether or not an answer is acceptable, leading to variability. 25-way annotations on 302 examples show that for items where >80% of annotators gave a non-null answer, expert judgments agree they are overwhelmingly correct. Disagreement is largely accounted for by 'Correct but debatable' cases. Long/short answers have 90%/84% precision respectively.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 for training examples, 5 for development and test examples, 25 for a subset of 302 examples
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: A solution to NQ will have genuine utility and is better equipped as a benchmark for NLU. Closing the gap between baselines and human upper bounds will require significant advances in NLU.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: There may be biases in the choice to focus on Wikipedia as the source of factual information.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Focuses on longer queries (8 words or more), excluding shorter queries. Excludes 'how to' questions. Limited to Wikipedia domain. The model struggles to learn from list-formatted data which makes up only 6% of non-null examples.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training data for the QA problem, research in natural language understanding, studying human performance in providing QA annotations, benchmark for evaluating question answering systems.
